doc.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Sight-reading a hard part for John Williams's Missouri Breaks
summary: Studio dates were sight-read, but John Williams's film part for him and Jay Berliner was supplied the night before.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. So when you’d come to the studio for a date, you would not have seen the music beforehand is that right?
Not really, no. A couple of times the contractor knew it was very difficult music. And one time John Williams came to New York to do a movie called — well John Williams came to New York.

“Missouri Breaks” it was called. And he had written, the contractor thought, a very difficult part for me and Jay. It was like, you know the country group Flat and Scruggs? One of those real long country solos, in harmony you know. And so he got us the part the night before. And I was really grateful. Because John Williams — yeah I wish I’d even done a better job. John was great though. It really was marvelous.
